newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WALSH SENDS AUSTRALIA INTO TAILSPIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WALSH SENDS AUSTRALIA INTO TAILSPIN.

text.p: West Indies captain Courtney Walsh sent Australia crashing towards a possible innings defeat as relations between the two sides deteriorated badly in the fifth and final test on Monday.
Walsh bowled unchanged through the afternoon session to claim five wickets despite the handicap of a hamstring injury as Australia collapsed in their second innings at the WACA Ground.
At tea on the third day, Australia were 133 for eight, still needing to score another eight runs to make the tourists bat again.
West Indies, who began the day on 353 for seven in reply to Australia's first innings 243, were dismissed before lunch for 384, a lead of 141 runs.
Umpires Peter Willey and Darrell Hair were forced to intervene late in the West Indies' innings to bring together captains Mark Taylor and Walsh to warn them about their players' poor behaviour.
Relations between the two camps soured on Sunday when West Indies vice-captain and star batsman Brian Lara accused the Australians of persistent sledging.
Lara, who scored his first century of the series on Sunday, was on the field as a runner for Walsh when the umpires stepped in to call the captains together.

"They (the umpires) called the two captains together and said it stops now or there shall be a report. It did stop and I am happy with that," International Cricket Council match referee Raman Subba Row said in a statement released by the Australian Cricket Board.

Even though he was inconvenienced in his batting, the veteran paceman was able to bowl off a shortened run and fully exploited the wicket's extremely variable bounce to dismiss Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Paul Reiffel and wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
Although Australia came into the match with an unassailable 3-1 lead in the series under his leadership, Taylor completed a miserable season as a batsman when he was dismissed for one.
The left-handed opener has averaged just 17 in five test matches against the West Indies.
Fellow opener Hayden was the only batsman to offer resistance before he was trapped leg before wicket for 47 by off-spinner Carl Hooper.
Fast bowler Curtly Ambrose took two wickets to add to his five-wicket haul in the first innings despite aggravating a thigh injury on Monday.
